references.text: Samuel warns the people about the nature of kingship but affirms that the Lord is their true king, as Gideon points out here.
Samuel reminds the people that the Lord is their king, the same principle Gideon expresses when he refuses to rule over Israel.
The people reject God as their king by asking for a human king, in contrast to Gideon's acknowledgment of the Lord's sovereignty.
The Lord as judge, lawgiver, and king over His people confirms the same theocratic principle that Gideon expresses.
The Lord shall be king forever and ever, an eternal truth that Gideon acknowledges by refusing human kingship.
The Lord shall reign forever and ever, the foundation of Gideon's declaration that only the Lord should rule over Israel.
